introduction_markdown:
Multiple choice paper (0515 Chemistry 1, June 2020, Ordinary Level, one and a half hours). Answer ALL 50 questions. Each question has four suggested answers A, B, C and D; mark only one answer for each question. Calculators are allowed.

**Useful data:** relative atomic masses H = 1.0, C = 12.0, O = 16.0, Na = 23.0, K = 39.0, S = 32.0, Cu = 64.0; 1 faraday = 96000 coulombs; molar volume of any gas at r.t.p. = $24000\ \mathrm{cm^3}$; molar volume of any gas at s.t.p. = $22400\ \mathrm{cm^3}$; Avogadro number = $6.02\times 10^{23}$; specific heat capacity of water = $4.2\ \mathrm{J\ g^{-1}\ ^\circ C^{-1}}$.
enonce_intro_markdown: **Multiple choice questions** - choose the one correct answer, A, B, C or D.

questions.enonce_markdown: A uniform mixture of a solute and solvent is called
questions.corrige_markdown: A solute dissolved in a solvent gives a uniform (homogeneous) mixture, and that mixture is simply called a **solution**. The other options describe special cases: an aqueous solution is one whose solvent is water, a standard solution is one of accurately known concentration, and a saturated solution is one that cannot dissolve any more solute at that temperature. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following elements is stored under paraffin oil?
questions.corrige_markdown: Potassium is a very reactive Group I metal: it reacts quickly with oxygen and moisture in the air, so it is kept under paraffin oil. Phosphorus (white phosphorus) is stored under water, while aluminium and zinc do not need any special storage. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: What name is given to the reaction that occurs when hydrochloric acid and potassium hydroxide react?
questions.corrige_markdown: An acid reacting with a base (alkali) to give a salt and water is a **neutralization** reaction: $\mathrm{HCl(aq) + KOH(aq) \rightarrow KCl(aq) + H_2O(l)}$. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following pairs constitutes a major cause of acid rain?
questions.corrige_markdown: Acid rain is caused by the acidic oxides of sulphur and nitrogen. $\mathrm{SO_2}$ forms sulphurous/sulphuric acid and $\mathrm{NO_2}$ forms nitric acid with rain water. $\mathrm{CO_2}$ is only weakly acidic and $\mathrm{CO}$ is a neutral oxide, which rules out A, B and C. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify the hydrocarbon which will rapidly decolourize bromine water when it is bubbled through it.
questions.corrige_markdown: Only an unsaturated hydrocarbon (one with a $\mathrm{C=C}$ double bond) rapidly decolourizes bromine water, by an addition reaction. Propene, $\mathrm{CH_3CH=CH_2}$, is the only alkene in the list; ethane, butane and propane are saturated alkanes and do not react rapidly. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following reactions will NOT occur?
questions.corrige_markdown: A halogen displaces a less reactive halogen from a solution of its halide. Reactivity falls down the group: $\mathrm{Cl_2 > Br_2 > I_2}$. So $\mathrm{Cl_2}$ displaces both $\mathrm{I^-}$ (A) and $\mathrm{Br^-}$ (D), and $\mathrm{Br_2}$ displaces $\mathrm{I^-}$ (B). In C, iodine (the least reactive) would have to displace bromine from KBr, which cannot happen. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify an enzyme that catalyzes the conversion of glucose to ethanol
questions.corrige_markdown: Fermentation of glucose to ethanol and carbon dioxide is catalysed by **zymase** (found in yeast): $\mathrm{C_6H_{12}O_6 \rightarrow 2C_2H_5OH + 2CO_2}$. Diastase and maltase break down starch/maltose, and invertase converts sucrose to glucose and fructose. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Calculate the percentage by mass of water of crystallization in hydrated copper(II) sulphate, $\mathrm{CuSO_4.5H_2O}$. (RMM = 250)
questions.corrige_markdown: Five molecules of water of crystallization have mass $5 \times (2\times 1.0 + 16.0) = 5\times 18 = 90$. Percentage of water $= \frac{90}{250}\times 100 = 36.0\%$. The other options do not correspond to 5 molecules of water in a formula mass of 250. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Equilibrium is said to be attained when:
questions.corrige_markdown: A reversible reaction is at equilibrium when the **rate of the forward reaction equals the rate of the backward reaction**, so the concentrations stay constant. Option B is a trap: the forward and backward reactions take place at the same time even before equilibrium is reached, so that statement is true of any reversible reaction and is not the condition for equilibrium. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: the forward and backward reactions are taking place at the same time
the rate of forward and backward reactions is the same.
reactants are being used up at the same time

questions.enonce_markdown: Determine the oxidation state of iron in $\mathrm{Fe_2O_3}$
questions.corrige_markdown: The compound is neutral and oxygen is $-2$. Let the oxidation state of Fe be $x$: $2x + 3(-2) = 0$, so $x = +3$. Option D ("3") has no sign, and an oxidation state is always written with its sign. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Select the appropriate reagents and reaction conditions for the preparation of $\mathrm{Cl_2}$ in the laboratory.
questions.corrige_markdown: Chlorine is made by oxidising chloride ions. Concentrated sulphuric acid and sodium chloride give hydrogen chloride, and the oxidising agent manganese(IV) oxide, with heating, oxidises the chloride to chlorine: $\mathrm{2NaCl + 2H_2SO_4 + MnO_2 \rightarrow Na_2SO_4 + MnSO_4 + 2H_2O + Cl_2}$. Option A has no source of chloride; C has no oxidising agent (only HCl gas is formed); D has no oxidising agent either, and concentrated HCl with sulphuric acid alone does not give chlorine. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: $\mathrm{NH_3}$ is collected in the laboratory
questions.corrige_markdown: Ammonia is much less dense than air and extremely soluble in water, so it cannot be collected over water (D). It is collected **by upward delivery**, that is by downward displacement of air: the gas jar is held upside down and the gas rises into it. "Downward delivery" (upward displacement of air) is used for gases denser than air such as $\mathrm{Cl_2}$, $\mathrm{CO_2}$ and HCl. **Answer: A.**

**13.** An irritating gas which bleaches damp litmus paper
questions.corrige_markdown: Damp litmus paper is bleached by chlorine: $\mathrm{Cl_2 + H_2O \rightarrow HCl + HOCl}$, and the hypochlorous acid formed destroys the colour. Chlorine is also a pungent, irritating gas. HCl is irritating too but only turns damp blue litmus red without bleaching it. **Answer: D.**

A. $\mathrm{CO}$

B. HCl

C. $\mathrm{CO_2}$

D. $\mathrm{Cl_2}$

*Each gas could be selected once, more than once or not at all.*

**14.** A colourless, tasteless, poisonous gas
questions.corrige_markdown: Carbon monoxide, CO, is colourless, odourless and tasteless and is poisonous because it combines with haemoglobin in the blood. HCl and $\mathrm{Cl_2}$ have strong smells, and $\mathrm{CO_2}$ is not poisonous. **Answer: A.**

**15.** A gas used in fire extinguishers
questions.corrige_markdown: Carbon dioxide is denser than air and does not support combustion, so it smothers a fire; it is used in fire extinguishers. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: What mass of solid $\mathrm{Na_2CO_3}$ is needed to prepare $250\ \mathrm{cm^3}$ of $0.1\ \mathrm{M}$ $\mathrm{Na_2CO_3(aq)}$? (RMM $\mathrm{Na_2CO_3}$ = 106)
questions.corrige_markdown: Amount of $\mathrm{Na_2CO_3}$ $= 0.1\ \mathrm{mol\ dm^{-3}} \times \frac{250}{1000}\ \mathrm{dm^3} = 0.025\ \mathrm{mol}$. Mass $= 0.025 \times 106 = 2.65\ \mathrm{g}$. Option C (0.025) is the number of moles, not the mass; B and D come from errors in converting the volume. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which one of the following is an amphoteric oxide?
questions.corrige_markdown: An amphoteric oxide reacts with both acids and bases. Aluminium oxide does: $\mathrm{Al_2O_3 + 6HCl \rightarrow 2AlCl_3 + 3H_2O}$ and $\mathrm{Al_2O_3 + 2NaOH + 3H_2O \rightarrow 2NaAl(OH)_4}$. $\mathrm{Na_2O}$ is basic, $\mathrm{NO_2}$ is acidic and $\mathrm{CO}$ is neutral. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Select a property of a covalent compound:
questions.corrige_markdown: Covalent compounds are made of discrete **molecules** held by shared pairs of electrons. They do not contain ions, so they are not electrolytes and do not conduct electricity in the solid state. Options A, B and D are properties of ionic compounds. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: A conductor in the solid state

questions.enonce_markdown:
Choose a pair of electronic configurations that represents two metal atoms in the same period of the periodic table

| | Atom 1 | Atom 2 |
|---|---|---|
| A | 2,3 | 2,4 |
| B | 2,8,1 | 2,8,5 |
| C | 2,8,8 | 2,8,7 |
| D | 2,8,8,1 | 2,8,8,2 |
questions.corrige_markdown: The number of shells gives the period, and the number of outer electrons gives the group. A: 2,3 and 2,4 are boron and carbon (period 2), both non-metals/metalloid. B: 2,8,1 is sodium (metal) but 2,8,5 is phosphorus (non-metal). C: 2,8,8 is argon and 2,8,7 is chlorine, both non-metals. D: 2,8,8,1 is potassium and 2,8,8,2 is calcium, both metals in period 4. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Condensation is a change of state from:
questions.corrige_markdown: Condensation is the change of a gas (vapour) into a liquid when it is cooled. Liquid to gas is evaporation or boiling, and solid to gas is sublimation. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Charles' law can be represented mathematically as:
questions.corrige_markdown: Charles' law states that, at constant pressure, the volume of a fixed mass of gas is directly proportional to its absolute (kelvin) temperature: $V \propto T$. Option A, $P \propto \frac{1}{V}$, is Boyle's law (the trap); B and D do not describe either law. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: In which of these substances can hydrogen bonding occur?
questions.corrige_markdown: Hydrogen bonding needs a hydrogen atom bonded to a very electronegative atom (F, O or N). In water, H is bonded to O, so the molecules form hydrogen bonds with each other. Oxygen and hydrogen gases have non-polar molecules, and helium consists of single atoms. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Calculate the quantity of electricity in coulombs used when a current of $1.5\ \mathrm{A}$ is passed through an electrolyte for 1 hour 20 mins.
questions.corrige_markdown: Time $= 1\ \mathrm{h}\ 20\ \mathrm{min} = 80\ \mathrm{min} = 80\times 60 = 4800\ \mathrm{s}$. Quantity of electricity $Q = I\,t = 1.5 \times 4800 = 7200\ \mathrm{C}$. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The following substances are deliquescent EXCEPT
questions.corrige_markdown: Deliquescent substances absorb so much water from the air that they dissolve in it. Sodium hydroxide, magnesium chloride and calcium chloride are all deliquescent. Potassium chloride is not: it stays dry in the air. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: What happens when a few drops of water are added to anhydrous copper(II) Sulphate?
questions.corrige_markdown: Anhydrous copper(II) sulphate is a white powder. When water is added to it, it forms the hydrated salt, which is blue: $\mathrm{CuSO_4(s) + 5H_2O(l) \rightarrow CuSO_4.5H_2O(s)}$ (white to blue). This is used as a test for water. Options A and C describe the blue hydrated salt, not the anhydrous one. **Answer: D.**

choix.texte: The blue crystals dissolve in water
The white powder does not dissolve in water
The blue crystals crumble to form a white paste
The white powder turns into blue crystals

questions.enonce_markdown: If the first and second burette readings during a titration are $5\ \mathrm{cm^3}$ and $17.3\ \mathrm{cm^3}$ respectively. Determine the volume of liquid used to reach the end point.
questions.corrige_markdown: The volume used is the final reading minus the initial reading: $17.3 - 5.0 = 12.3\ \mathrm{cm^3}$. Option B adds the readings, and A and D give only one reading. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
*Questions 31 - 32.* Study the table below which concerns some chemical tests performed on solutions of salt X and salt Y, and then answer the questions that follow:

| Salt | Colour of solution | Flame test | Adding dilute HCl | Adding $\mathrm{BaCl_2}$(aq) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X | Colourless | Golden yellow flame | Effervescence, turns lime water milky | White ppt |
| Y | Colourless | Brick red | No effect | White ppt |

**31.** Identify the cation and the gas given off for salt X
questions.corrige_markdown: The golden yellow flame shows sodium ions, $\mathrm{Na^+}$ (calcium would give a brick red flame). Effervescence with dilute HCl, with a gas that turns lime water milky, shows a carbonate giving off carbon dioxide: $\mathrm{CO_3^{2-} + 2H^+ \rightarrow H_2O + CO_2}$. Salt X is sodium carbonate. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
*Questions 31 - 32.* Study the table below which concerns some chemical tests performed on solutions of salt X and salt Y, and then answer the questions that follow:

| Salt | Colour of solution | Flame test | Adding dilute HCl | Adding $\mathrm{BaCl_2}$(aq) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X | Colourless | Golden yellow flame | Effervescence, turns lime water milky | White ppt |
| Y | Colourless | Brick red | No effect | White ppt |

**32.** Identify salt Y
questions.corrige_markdown: The brick red flame shows $\mathrm{Ca^{2+}}$, so Y is a calcium salt: A and B (sodium salts) are out. No effect with dilute HCl means it is not a carbonate. A white precipitate with $\mathrm{BaCl_2}$(aq) shows sulphate ions, $\mathrm{Ba^{2+} + SO_4^{2-} \rightarrow BaSO_4}$; calcium chloride would not give a precipitate with barium chloride. Y is calcium sulphate. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A compound contains 85.5% C and 14.3% H only. Determine its empirical formula.
questions.corrige_markdown: Divide each percentage by the relative atomic mass: C: $85.5 \div 12.0 = 7.125$; H: $14.3 \div 1.0 = 14.3$. Divide by the smaller: C: $1$; H: $14.3 \div 7.125 = 2.0$. The simplest ratio C : H is $1 : 2$, so the empirical formula is $\mathrm{CH_2}$. Option A, $\mathrm{C_2H_4}$, has the right ratio but is a molecular formula, not the simplest whole-number ratio. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A mole of $\mathrm{CO_2}$
questions.corrige_markdown: One mole of any gas occupies $24000\ \mathrm{cm^3}$ ($24\ \mathrm{dm^3}$) at r.t.p. and $22400\ \mathrm{cm^3}$ ($22.4\ \mathrm{dm^3}$) at s.t.p., and contains $6.02\times 10^{23}$ molecules. A: one mole of $\mathrm{CO_2}$ has mass $12.0 + 2\times 16.0 = 44\ \mathrm{g}$, not 1 g. C: $24\ \mathrm{dm^3}$ is the r.t.p. volume; at s.t.p. it is $22.4\ \mathrm{dm^3}$. D: the number is $10^{23}$, not $10^{22}$. Only B is correct. **Answer: B.**

Limestone (calcium carbonate) is used as a flux in the blast furnace to remove silica as slag (1), as a raw material with sand and soda for glass (2), and with clay to make cement (3). Aluminium is extracted by electrolysis of alumina dissolved in cryolite, and calcium carbonate is not used (4 is wrong). So 1, 2 and 3 only. **Answer: A.**

The main greenhouse gases that cause global warming are methane (2) and carbon dioxide (4). Sulphur dioxide causes acid rain, not global warming (1 is wrong). Ozone is the gas of the ozone layer, which is thinned by CFCs; it is not counted among the gases responsible for global warming at this level (3 is wrong). So 2 and 4 only. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
*Questions 35 - 37.* Each question is followed by four responses numbered 1-4. One or more of these responses is (are) correct. Decide which response(s) is(are) correct then choose:

A. if only 1, 2 and 3 are correct;

B. if only 1 and 3 are correct;

C. if only 2 and 4 are correct;

D. if only 4 is correct.

**37.** Consider the reaction:

$\mathrm{Zn(s) + 2HCl(aq) \rightarrow ZnCl_2(aq) + H_2(g)}$

The rate of the reaction will be affected by a change in:

1. temperature
2. surface area
3. concentration
4. light intensity
questions.corrige_markdown: The reaction of solid zinc with aqueous acid goes faster at higher temperature (1), when the zinc is in smaller pieces so that its surface area is larger (2), and with more concentrated acid (3). Light intensity has no effect on this reaction (4 is wrong). So 1, 2 and 3 only. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Select the electronic configuration of $^{39}_{19}K^{+}$ ion.
questions.corrige_markdown: A neutral potassium atom has 19 electrons: 2,8,8,1. The $\mathrm{K^+}$ ion has lost the outer electron, so it has 18 electrons: **2,8,8**. Options B and C have the wrong number of electrons (20 and 39), and A is not a valid configuration. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Determine the number of each type of atom present in $(\mathrm{NH_4})_3\mathrm{PO_4}$

| | No. of atoms of N | No. of atoms of H | No. of atoms of P | No. of atoms of O |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | 1 | 4 | 3 | 4 |
| B | 3 | 12 | 1 | 4 |
| C | 1 | 4 | 1 | 4 |
| D | 3 | 12 | 3 | 4 |
questions.corrige_markdown: The subscript 3 outside the bracket multiplies everything inside: $(\mathrm{NH_4})_3$ gives $3$ N and $3\times 4 = 12$ H. The $\mathrm{PO_4}$ part gives 1 P and 4 O. So the numbers are N = 3, H = 12, P = 1, O = 4. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The most abundant component of air is
questions.corrige_markdown: Dry air contains about 78% nitrogen and 21% oxygen, so **nitrogen** is the most abundant. Water vapour varies and is small, and helium is only a trace gas. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
The following equilibrium reaction represents the industrial production of ammonia.

$\mathrm{N_2(g) + 3H_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2NH_3(g)}$   $\Delta H = -92\ \mathrm{kJ\ mol^{-1}}$

If the temperature is increased, the equilibrium position will
questions.corrige_markdown: The forward reaction has $\Delta H = -92\ \mathrm{kJ\ mol^{-1}}$, so it is exothermic and the backward reaction is endothermic. By Le Chatelier's principle, raising the temperature favours the endothermic direction, which absorbs the extra heat. The equilibrium position shifts **to the left**, and less ammonia is present at equilibrium. **Answer: D.**

choix.texte: Shift to right then to the left

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following is an oxidizing agent used in the treatment of water?
questions.corrige_markdown: Chlorine, $\mathrm{Cl_2}$, is the oxidizing agent added to water to kill germs (disinfection). $\mathrm{Ca(OH)_2}$ is a base used to adjust acidity, and $\mathrm{MnO_2}$ is a laboratory oxidizing agent, not used in water treatment; hydrogen peroxide is an oxidizing agent too, but chlorine is the one used in the standard treatment of water. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Choose a characteristic of alkaline earth metals.
questions.corrige_markdown: Group II carbonates decompose on heating to the oxide and carbon dioxide, e.g. $\mathrm{CaCO_3 \rightarrow CaO + CO_2}$: C is correct. A: with nitrogen they form nitrides (e.g. $\mathrm{Mg_3N_2}$), not nitrites. B: their hydroxides decompose on heating to the oxide and water. D: their nitrates give the oxide, nitrogen dioxide and oxygen; it is the Group I nitrates that give nitrites and oxygen. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: They do form nitrites on combination with nitrogen.
Their hydroxides are stable to heat
Their nitrates decompose to nitrites and oxygen

questions.enonce_markdown: In an exothermic reaction,
questions.corrige_markdown: In an exothermic reaction heat is given out to the surroundings, so the surroundings get warmer and the reactants have more energy than the products ($\Delta H$ is negative). B and C describe an endothermic reaction. D is also the description of an endothermic reaction: more energy is needed to break bonds than is released on making new ones. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: the energy content of the reactants is more than that of the products
heat is absorbed from the environment.
the temperature of the environment drops after the reaction
the energy required to break bonds in reactants is greater than the energy released when new bonds are formed in products.

questions.enonce_markdown: Members of a homologous series have the following characteristics EXCEPT
questions.corrige_markdown: Members of a homologous series share a general formula, similar chemical properties and general methods of preparation. Their physical properties are not the same: they change gradually, for example boiling points rise as the chain gets longer. **Answer: D.**

choix.texte: Can be obtained by a general method of preparation

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following is not true of detergents?
questions.corrige_markdown: Detergents (soapless detergents) have cleansing properties (B), are made from petroleum products (C), and do not form scum with hard water (D). They are synthetic, not natural polymers, so A is the statement that is not true. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: are not affected by hard water

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following pH values best describes the pH of an aqueous solution of NaOH?
questions.corrige_markdown: Sodium hydroxide is a strong alkali, so its solution has a high pH, well above 7. Of the values given, 12 is the best description. pH 2 is strongly acidic, 7 is neutral, and 8 is only very weakly alkaline. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of these will burn with the most luminous and sooty flame?
questions.corrige_markdown: The higher the percentage of carbon in the fuel, the less completely it burns in air and the sootier the flame. Percentage of carbon: $\mathrm{C_3H_8}$: $\frac{36}{44} = 81.8\%$; $\mathrm{C_3H_4}$: $\frac{36}{40} = 90.0\%$; $\mathrm{C_4H_{10}}$: $\frac{48}{58} = 82.8\%$; $\mathrm{C_3H_7OH}$: $\frac{36}{60} = 60.0\%$. $\mathrm{C_3H_4}$ (an unsaturated hydrocarbon) is richest in carbon. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Why is it recommended to use a polythene cup in determining the heat of neutralization?
questions.corrige_markdown: Polythene is a poor conductor of heat (an insulator), so a polythene cup reduces the heat lost by conduction to the surroundings and the measured temperature rise is more accurate. Being transparent or unbreakable is not the reason for the choice. **Answer: D.**

choix.texte: It reduces heat loss by convection
It eases observation because it is transparent.
It will not break if it falls.
It reduces heat loss by conduction

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following fuels is most environmentally friendly?
questions.corrige_markdown: Hydrogen burns to give only water: $\mathrm{2H_2 + O_2 \rightarrow 2H_2O}$, with no carbon dioxide, carbon monoxide, sulphur dioxide or soot. Butane, coal and firewood all release carbon dioxide, and coal also gives sulphur dioxide. **Answer: A.**
